cards.text: This scene comes from the prophet Isaiah's message, and it opens with a question. Who is this coming from Edom, the land of the Edomites, Esau's descendants (Genesis 36:9), from Bozrah, one of its cities, with crimson-stained garments? Who is this robed in splendor?

cards.question: The One coming from Edom is robed in splendor. How is He marching?

answers.text: In the greatness of His strength
In the weariness of a long road
In the sorrow of a heavy heart

cards.text: Somebody asks who this is, then asks again, and I get it, because my eyebrows do that every time the bakery door swings open. The One from Edom answers for Himself: He is proclaiming vindication.

cards.question: The One from Edom says He is mighty to save.
Next comes a question about why the One from Edom's clothes are red. His garments look like the garments of someone who does what?

cards.text: The One from Edom answers that He has trodden the winepress alone. No one from the nations was with Him.
This part is heavy, friend. The One from Edom says He trampled them in His anger and trod them down in His fury, and their blood spattered His garments.

cards.question: The One from Edom says the day of ___ was in His heart.
Along with the day of vengeance, the One from Edom says the year of His redemption was still far off.

cards.text: Then the One from Edom says, "I looked…" He's looking for someone to help.

cards.question: When no one assisted the One from Edom, He says He was relieved.
With no one to help, what does the One from Edom say brought Him salvation?

cards.text: The One from Edom adds that His own wrath upheld Him. He finishes: He trampled the nations in His anger, made them drunk in His wrath and poured out their blood on the ground.
